target.title: fix(codex): resolve dynamic tool hard timeout from timeoutSeconds when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a dynamic tool call passes `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }`) but omits `timeoutMs`, both the primary and `/btw` side-thread hard-call timeout readers only looked at `timeoutMs` and fell back to the default 90s guard. Tools that explicitly set a longer timeout in seconds (e.g. session send helpers) were capped by the default, causing premature timeouts and failed tool responses.

Fixes [#98864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98864).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the primary (`dynamic-tool-execution.ts`) and side-thread (`side-question.ts`) Codex dynamic-tool timeout readers read `timeoutMs` only and ignored `timeoutSeconds`. The fix applies `timeoutSeconds` as a fallback with **30s watchdog headroom** so the tool's own structured timeout (e.g. `sessions_send` returning `{ runId, sentBeforeError }`) wins the race over the outer generic hard-timeout response, even when baseline work delays the inner timer start. Fractional `timeoutSeconds` values are rejected via `Number.isInteger` to match `sessions_send` integer validation.

### Behavior rules

| Priority | Input | Outcome |
|----------|-------|---------|
| 1 | `timeoutMs` is valid positive number | Use `timeoutMs` (no headroom, existing behavior) |
| 2 | `timeoutMs` absent/invalid, `timeoutSeconds` valid integer | Use `timeoutSeconds * 1000 + 30s headroom` (**new**) |
| 3 | `timeoutSeconds` is fractional or invalid | Ignored (matches `sessions_send` integer contract) |
| 4 | Both absent/invalid | Fall back to configured or default timeout (existing) |

## User Impact

- **Before**: Dynamic tool call `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }` -> reads `undefined` from `timeoutMs` -> falls back to 90s default -> tool times out prematurely. Affected both primary and `/btw` side-thread calls.
- **After**: Dynamic tool call `{ timeoutSeconds: 120 }` -> reads `150000` (120s + 30s headroom) -> watchdog gives the tool enough time to return its own structured result -> `sessions_send` structured `{ runId, sentBeforeError }` reaches caller before watchdog fires.

`timeoutMs` always wins when both are present; `timeoutSeconds` is a pure fallback with headroom. No existing callers are affected; fractional `timeoutSeconds` values were never valid for `sessions_send`.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (60/60 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
```

Primary path: +4 tests (fallback w/ 30s headroom, timeoutMs precedence, fractional rejection, invalid value)
Side-thread path: +3 tests (fallback w/ 30s headroom, timeoutMs precedence, fractional rejection)

### Real Machine Runtime Verification

**Environment**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0

```
Primary: timeoutSeconds=120     -> 150000 ✅
Primary: timeoutMs=30000+ts=120 -> 30000  ✅
Primary: timeoutSeconds=120.5   -> 90000  ✅ (fractional rejected)
Primary: no timeout fields      -> 90000  ✅ (default)

Side:    timeoutSeconds=120     -> 150000 ✅
Side:    timeoutMs=30000+ts=120 -> 30000  ✅
```

### Verification Summary

| Scenario | Primary | Side-thread |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `timeoutSeconds=120`, no `timeoutMs` | ✅ 150000 | ✅ 150000 |
| `timeoutMs=30000` + `timeoutSeconds=120` | ✅ 30000 (wins) | ✅ 30000 (wins) |
| Fractional `timeoutSeconds=120.5` | ✅ Default | ✅ Default |
| Neither field | ✅ Default | ✅ Default |

## Changes

| File | Changed | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| `dynamic-tool-execution.ts` | +30s headroom, timeoutSeconds fallback, integer-only guard | `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` + `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` |
| `side-question.ts` | Same pattern for `/btw` path | `readSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` + `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs` |
| `dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` | +4 tests | fallback, precedence, fractional, invalid |
| `side-question.test.ts` | +3 tests | fallback, precedence, fractional |
